Driving event

An identical problem had been previously discovered that prompted a change to the manufacturing procedures to include a specified torque for the mounting screws. The failed flight unit had been reworked, but the manufacturing procedural change had not been incorporated into the rework process.

Lesson

Transition of logistics functions under Phase 1 of the Space Flight Operations Contract (SFOC) appears to be taking place smoothly. Key personnel are maintaining continuity in management techniques and processes.

Recommendation

Continue adherence to established systems, and make maximum use of the inherent capability of the incumbent personnel in the logistics systems.

title: LLIS 1016: International Space Station (ISS) Program/Real-Time Operations/Collision Avoidance Maneuvers
snippet:
Driving event

Collision Avoidance Maneuvers of the ISS Require Close, Real-Time Cooperation Between NASA and US Space Command

Lesson

The collision avoidance and maneuver process for evading meteoroids and orbital debris is complicated and not yet completely worked out for many of the scenarios likely to occur during the life of the ISS program.

Recommendation

The collision avoidance and maneuver process must be worked out in detail and documented in interagency memoranda and in agreements among the international partners.

title: LLIS 1065: Space Shuttle Program/Operations-Processing/Workforce
snippet:
Driving event

Effects of Lack of Knowledge and Experience on Operations

Lesson

The combined effect of workforce downsizing, the recent hiring freeze, and the Shuttle Processing contract (SPC) transition, especially at KSC, has raised the possibility that NASA senior managers in the future will lack the necessary hands-on technical knowledge and in-line experience to provide effective insight of operations.

Recommendation

NASA should develop and promulgate training and career paths, with a special focus on providing hands-on technical knowledge and experience, so that NASA's future senior managers will possess the range of skills and experience required for effective insight of the SPC.

title: LLIS 1113: International Space Station (ISS) Program/Extravehicular Activity (EVA)/Simplified Aid for EVA Rescue (SAFER)
snippet:
Driving event

Lack of Sufficient Operational Assets to Procure Necessary Safety Hardware

Lesson

The EVA project lacks sufficient operational assets to meet unplanned contingencies. There are no spare Extravehicular Mobility Units (EMU's). Only five U.S. Simplified Aid for EVA Rescue (SAFER) flight units will be available to meet a requirement to maintain three units on orbit. In addition, only four Russian SAFER units are planned.

Recommendation

To meet contingencies that are almost certain to arise, additional EMU's and SAFER units or their critical long lead components should be procured as soon as possible.

Mission schedules can be disrupted if contingency time is not allowed for training on new mission-support hardware.

Lack of voice communications can have serious impact on the operations of a center and its safety services.
